extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on restriction practice and nonstatutory double patenting under 35 U.S.C. 111: when restriction is proper, how to determine distinctness/independence of claimed inventions, election and reply procedures, linking and rejoinder, and avoiding double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview and scope of MPEP Chapter 800 concerning restriction practice and double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for Restriction Practice in Statute and Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and rule-based foundations authorizing and constraining restriction practice under statutes and USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of "Independent" and "Distinct"
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and interpretive guidance on what constitutes independent inventions and distinct inventions for restriction and double patenting analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: What a restriction requirement is, its scope, and when it is used in examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction — When Proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and circumstances under which a restriction requirement is proper and should be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by Examiner with at Least Partial Signatory Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on who should review and sign restriction requirements and the required level of examiner authority for making such requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species Requirements – Markush Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and practice for electing species when claims include Markush groupings or multiple species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations for restriction practice in transitional applications (e.g., provisional to nonprovisional or other transitional contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Application — Linking Claim Allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: When a linking claim in a transitional application may be found allowable and its effect on restriction/election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Application — Generic Claim Allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: When a generic claim in a transitional application may be allowable and how that impacts restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide Sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction practice considerations specific to claims involving nucleotide sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue Application Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: How restriction and double patenting principles apply in the context of reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Double Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and distinctions between statutory and nonstatutory double patenting, and related concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of Nonstatutory Double Patenting Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. 121
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how 35 U.S.C. 121 affects nonstatutory double patenting rejections and when such rejections are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding a Double Patenting Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices and filing/claim strategies to avoid nonstatutory double patenting rejections (e.g., terminal disclaimers, claim amendments, divisional practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commonly Owned Inventions of Different Inventive Entities; Non-Commonly Owned Inventions Subject to a Joint Research Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: How ownership and joint research agreements affect double patenting analysis and possible defenses or exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Technology Center Director
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how matters related to restriction or double patenting should be escalated to the Technology Center Director for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Patent Term Extension under 35 U.S.C. 156 on Nonstatutory Double Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: How patent term extension considerations interact with nonstatutory double patenting determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Improper Joinder in Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences and corrective measures when claims improperly join distinct inventions in a single patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Distinctness or Independence of Claimed Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: General approach and criteria for determining whether claimed inventions are distinct or independent for restriction/double patenting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare Claimed Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative analysis of claimed subject matter to assess distinctness/independence between claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Embodiment, Claims Defining Same Essential Features
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when multiple claims define the same essential features of a single embodiment and implications for restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus and/or Species Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing genus claims vs species claims and how they affect restriction and double patenting analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species May Be Independent or Related Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for when species within a genus are considered independent inventions versus merely related/obvious variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Generic Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a generic claim (genus) and how to treat such claims in restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Limited to Species
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of claims that are limited to particular species and their relationship to broader generic claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction Between Mutually Exclusive Species
rubrics_metrics.description: When mutually exclusive species justify a restriction requirement between species claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species Must Be Patentably Distinct From Each Other
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that species be patentably distinct from each other to avoid restriction or to justify separate claims/applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic Claims Presented In a Separate Application After Issuance of Species Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice and consequences when a generic claim is filed in a later application after species claims have issued in an earlier patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: How related inventions (combinations, subcombinations, processes, products) are analyzed for restriction and distinctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination and Subcombination
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for distinguishing combination claims from subcombination claims and implications for restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria of Distinctness Between Combination and Subcombination
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factors to determine distinctness between a combination invention and its subcombinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations Usable Together
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether subcombinations are designed to be usable together and how that affects distinctness and restriction decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and Apparatus for Its Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of claims to a process and to an apparatus for practicing that process, and whether they are distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process of Making and Product Made
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between claims to a process of making a product and claims to the product itself, for restriction/double patenting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and Product Made
rubrics_metrics.description: How apparatus claims and claims to products made by the apparatus are treated regarding distinctness and restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and Process of Using
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of product claims versus claims to using the product; considerations for restriction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product, Process of Making, and Process of Using
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis when claims include product, process of making the product, and process of using the product together in one application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Products; Related Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: How related products and related processes are evaluated for distinctness and restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and identification of inventions that are independent of one another for the purposes of restriction and patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Report Practice Has No Effect on Restriction Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that the patentability report practice (e.g., TC reports) does not alter the standards or application of restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for Insisting Upon Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible reasons and policy rationales the Office uses to insist upon a restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for Holding of Independence or Distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factual or legal bases for finding inventions independent or distinct in the examiner's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing Burden
rubrics_metrics.description: How the burden of proof/responsibility is allocated between the examiner and applicant when asserting or contesting restriction and distinctness determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Concept of linking claims (claims that link otherwise distinct inventions) and their effect on election and restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances in which an election of species is mandatory and how that election must be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election in Reply to a Restriction Requirement: Express
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for an express election in reply to a restriction requirement, including form and content rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Must be Complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that a reply to a restriction requirement must be complete to be proper — i.e., include necessary statements and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election is Required, Even When Requirement Is Traversed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule that an election must still be made even if the applicant traverses (disagrees with) the restriction requirement to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse is Required To Preserve Right of Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must traverse a restriction requirement to preserve the right to petition the requirement; guidance on how to traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse of Restriction Requirement With Linking Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations when traversing a restriction requirement that involves linking claims between inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election Other Than Express
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of election other than an express election (e.g., by originally presented claims, cancellation) and how they are treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election By Originally Presented Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original set of claims amounts to an election of certain inventions or species and the effect of that implied election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic Claims Only — No Election of Species; Linking Claims Only – No Election of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where only generic claims are presented (no species election required) and when linking claims do not necessitate an election of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election By Optional Cancelation of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: How optional cancellation of claims can serve as an election and the requirements for such an election to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election By Cancelation of Claims, Lacking Express Election Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: When cancellation of claims without an express election statement may nonetheless constitute an election and the consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Generally Does Not Permit Shift
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy that the Office will generally not permit an applicant to shift the election to a different invention after making an election, with exceptions noted in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate Exactly How Application Is To Be Restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the restriction requirement must precisely indicate how the application is to be restricted (which claims/inventions are grouped and how).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Requirement Complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The restriction requirement must be complete — specifying groups, elected invention, and other necessary procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline of Letter for Restriction Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested outline or form language for drafting a restriction requirement letter to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance on making elections and filing replies to restriction requirements including timing and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when the examiner should take action on the merits (e.g., examine the elected invention) after an election is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Making Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing rules and deadlines for making restriction requirements during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Requirement After Compliance With Preceding Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner may issue a new restriction requirement after an applicant has complied with a prior requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeating After Withdrawal Proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances under which repeating a restriction requirement after withdrawal of claims or withdrawal of an election is proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper Even Though Grouped Together in Parent Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance that a restriction requirement may be proper even if the inventions were previously grouped together in a parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Make the Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which examiners or officials are authorized and appropriate to make restriction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Restriction Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and limitations on making restriction requirements or handling elections via telephone communications with applicants/attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Claims Held To Be Drawn to Nonelected Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: How claims that are held to be directed to nonelected inventions are treated (e.g., withdrawn, allowed in a divisional, held in abeyance).

rubrics_metrics.name: After Election With Traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures applicable to claims after an applicant elects an invention while traversing the restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: After Election Without Traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures applicable after an applicant elects without traversing the restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for Different Invention Added After an Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle claims that claim a different invention that are added after an office action (e.g., restriction, new issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and process for rejoinder — reuniting claims to a previously nonelected invention when conditions change (e.g., allowable claims appear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder Between Product Inventions; Rejoinder Between Process Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance on rejoinder when the inventions are product-to-product or process-to-process relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of Process Requiring an Allowable Product
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejoinder of process claims requires that a product claim be found allowable before rejoinder is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims to Inventions That Are Not Patentably Distinct in Plural Applications of Same Applicant or Assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle claims that are not patentably distinct when they appear in plural applications of the same applicant or assignee (e.g., double patenting concerns across filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Invention Under the Patent Cooperation Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison and interplay between U.S. restriction practice and the PCT concept of unity of invention, and implications for international filings.
